package_info.package_name: N/A (npm registry infrastructure flaw, not a specific package)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (affects registry, not a package version)
package_info.why_malicious: The flaws enabled exposure of private package names (enabling targeted dependency confusion and typosquatting attacks) and allowed unauthorized users to publish new versions of any npm package, potentially enabling supply chain attacks.

required_permissions: read access to public npm replica feed

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Records containing names of private scoped npm packages (e.g., "@owner/package") were published to the public changes feed during maintenance.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During registry maintenance, the system exposed the names of private npm packages in the public replication feed, allowing any consumer of replicate.npmjs.com to enumerate private package names.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Private package names are intended to be confidential; their exposure enables targeted attacks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior is that private package names are never exposed to the public; here, they were leaked.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Public package names are routinely listed for legitimate discovery.
key_indicators: Private package names appearing in public feeds

execution_context.file_location: npm registry microservices (authorization and publishing services)
required_permissions: ability to upload a package to npm registry

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: A request to publish a new version of a package was authorized for one package (based on URL path), but the actual update was performed for a different package (based on uploaded package file contents), due to inconsistent validation between services.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During package publish, the authorization service validated user rights for one package, but the publishing service updated a different package based on the uploaded file, allowing unauthorized publication of new versions of any package.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This allows attackers to publish malicious updates to packages they do not own, a classic supply chain attack vector.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior is that only authorized maintainers can publish new versions of a package; here, any user could publish to any package.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; cross-package publishing is never legitimate.
key_indicators: Authorization and publishing services using different sources for package identity
Ability to publish to packages without ownership

attack_chain.action: Private package names are leaked to the public replication feed.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attackers enumerate private package names for targeted attacks.

attack_chain.action: Attackers use leaked names to perform dependency confusion or typosquatting attacks.
attack_chain.leads_to: Victims install malicious packages with similar or identical names.

attack_chain.action: Attackers exploit the authorization flaw to publish new versions of legitimate packages they do not own.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is distributed via trusted package names.

attack_chain.action: Victims install or update to malicious package versions, leading to compromise.
attack_chain.leads_to: Final goal: supply chain compromise of downstream consumers.

behavioral_signatures: Enumeration of private package names from public feeds
Unexpected publication of new versions by non-maintainers
Sudden appearance of new package versions from previously unseen accounts
file_indicators: Presence of private scoped package names (e.g., '@owner/package') in public replication feeds
Package version history showing unexpected publisher changes
network_indicators: Access to replicate.npmjs.com for bulk package name enumeration
Unusual API calls to npm registry for package publish actions
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor public npm replication feeds for the presence of private package names. Audit package version histories for unexpected publisher accounts. Alert on publish actions where the publisher is not a listed maintainer. Monitor for bulk access to replicate.npmjs.com and for patterns consistent with dependency confusion or typosquatting attacks.
